classification.difficultyReason: Identify the known and unknown sides relative to each marked angle, select sine, cosine or tangent, and multiply by the known side. Rotated diagrams require side recognition but no linked construction.

questions.mappingNote: All six unknowns are numerator sides: sine in a and e, cosine in b, and tangent in c, d and f. The directly assessed skill is finding a side using trigonometry.
questions.methodNote: Use SOHCAHTOA to select the ratio, substitute the given side and angle, rearrange by multiplication and round the final side to two decimal places, following Example 2.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select sine, cosine or tangent and calculate an unknown numerator side in a right-angled triangle.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the hypotenuse and the relevant sine or cosine ratio, then rearrange with the unknown in the denominator. Each part directly applies the taught side-finding procedure.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a and b use sine with an unknown hypotenuse; parts c and d use cosine with an unknown hypotenuse. The directly assessed skill is finding an unknown side in the denominator.
questions.methodNote: Identify opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to the given angle. Substitute into sine or cosine, multiply by the unknown denominator, then divide by the trigonometric ratio, as demonstrated by the denominator rearrangement in Example 2d. Keep calculator precision until rounding to two decimal places.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select sine or cosine and rearrange a ratio with the unknown hypotenuse in the denominator.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the two supplied sides relative to theta, select the appropriate ratio and apply its inverse. Different triangle orientations do not introduce an additional mathematical step.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts assess finding a right-triangle angle from two side lengths; trig-find-angle directly matches this task. Parts a/e use sine, b/d cosine and c/f tangent.
questions.methodNote: Identify opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to theta; substitute into sine, cosine or tangent, then use the corresponding inverse function in degree mode and round to one decimal place, as demonstrated in Example 3 on page 4.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select a basic right-triangle ratio from two supplied sides and apply its inverse.

classification.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate ratio across nine differently oriented right triangles, including unknown denominators and inverse ratios.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a, d and i find numerator sides; c, g and h find denominator sides; b, e and f use inverse ratios. The denominator-side skill is the most advanced directly assessed side-solving procedure, with numerator-side and angle skills secondary.
questions.methodNote: Use sine, cosine or tangent according to opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse. Example 2 demonstrates substitution and multiplication, and multiplying through by an unknown denominator before dividing by the ratio. Example 3 demonstrates inverse trigonometric functions for angles. Retain exact calculator expressions until the requested rounding.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate ratio across nine differently oriented right triangles, including unknown denominators and inverse ratios.

classification.difficultyReason: Complete right triangles by selecting side and inverse trigonometric ratios, using Pythagoras where appropriate and applying two rounding precisions.

questions.mappingNote: Page 2 defines the ratios and complementary angles; page 3 Example 2 demonstrates numerator and denominator side calculations; page 4 Example 3 demonstrates inverse trigonometry with one-decimal-place angles. Question 5 combines those methods to complete each triangle.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete right triangles by selecting side and inverse trigonometric ratios, using Pythagoras where appropriate and applying two rounding precisions.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute exact trigonometric ratios into compound expressions, simplify surds and rationalise denominators.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute exact trigonometric ratios into compound expressions, simplify surds and rationalise denominators.
